name: Grimace Shake
blurb: The 2023 TikTok trend of sipping McDonald's purple shake, then faking a horror scene
title: Grimace Shake Meme: Meaning, Origin & the TikTok Trend
description: The Grimace Shake trend began in June 2023: TikTokers wished McDonald's Grimace a happy birthday, sipped his purple shake and faked horror scenes.
h1: What is the Grimace Shake trend?
answer: The Grimace Shake trend is a 2023 TikTok joke built on McDonald's purple, berry-flavoured Grimace Birthday Shake, sold in the US from 12 June to 9 July 2023. Creators wish Grimace a happy birthday, take a sip, then cut to a staged "horror" scene: lying motionless with purple shake splattered around them or acting possessed. Austin Frazier (@thefrazmaz) posted the first such video in mid-June 2023, and the hashtag passed a billion views within a month.

body: Each video opens cheerfully: "Happy birthday, Grimace!" and a first sip. Then the tone flips to found-footage horror: the creator is shown collapsed on the floor or somewhere odd, with the purple shake spilled around them, as if a camera had found the aftermath. The joke is a parody of horror films, not a real reaction to the drink.

body.note: The shake is an ordinary milkshake and the scenes are staged. Grimace himself is a McDonald's mascot who debuted in 1971 as "Evil Grimace", a four-armed milkshake thief, before becoming the friendly purple blob.

head: Date
Event
rows: McDonald's starts selling the Grimace Birthday Shake in the US for the mascot's "birthday".
Austin Frazier posts the first trend video (dated 13 June by Know Your Meme, 14 June by McDonald's); it passes 2.6 million views.
McDonald's acknowledges the trend with a playful post in which Grimace pretends not to notice it.
The shake leaves US menus; by 12 July the hashtag has more than one billion TikTok views.
The shake returns in other markets, including Canada (May), the UK and Ireland (August) and Japan (October).

ul: The classic format: "Happy birthday Grimace!" sip, smash cut, staged crime scene.
Horror-movie style edits with eerie music, slow zooms and "found footage" captions.
Copycat videos staged in ever stranger places, each trying to top the last.
Comment jokes such as "he was never seen again after the first sip".

body: The trend peaked in June and July 2023 and is now a well-remembered summer meme. It is often cited as a viral marketing hit that the brand did not plan: McDonald's social media director said the trend was unexpected and that joining in too much had seemed risky, since the campaign was already working.

faq.a: No. It is a regular berry-flavoured milkshake; the videos are staged parodies of horror films.

faq.q: Who started the Grimace Shake trend?
faq.a: TikTok user Austin Frazier (@thefrazmaz), with a video in mid-June 2023.
A purple McDonald's mascot introduced in 1971, originally as "Evil Grimace", who stole milkshakes.
